test.name: Triage surfaces only pending hints, each with FamilySearch's confidence
test.description: Patrick Flynn (FamilySearch LZNY-BRF) has one accepted record match (the 1850 census) and three pending ones: the 1870 census (confidence 3) and the 1880 census (confidence 2), both new to the project, and the 1908 death certificate (confidence 2), which the project already extracted as src_004 — FamilySearch keeps it pending because nothing here writes back. Triage must ask for status ["pending"], surface only the three hints with their confidences, and report the death certificate as already linked (pe_005) rather than recommending it for extraction again. The pending-only fixture is listed first and the mixed one second, so a call without status gets the accepted match mixed in. Triage writes nothing (issue #2029).

input.delegation:
Check the FamilySearch hints on Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF, and tell me which look valid.

personId: LZNY-BRF
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The three pending hints are the 1870 census (M70C, confidence 3), the 1880 census (M80C, confidence 2) and the 1908 death certificate (MDEF, confidence 2). The 1850 census is an ACCEPTED match: the pending-only listing does not return it, and it should not get a Hint line of its own
Each hint's FamilySearch confidence (1-5) must be stated, and must not be the sole reason for its recommendation

The death certificate IS one of the three pending hints: FamilySearch keeps it pending because nothing here writes back. It is already linked: extracted as src_004 (log_005) and linked to Patrick by pe_005. Listing it with the line 'already linked' and no recommendation is the correct handling and is not presenting an accepted match; giving it a fresh accept would send it to a second extraction

The 1870 census agrees with the tree on name, age, birthplace, county and father. The 1880 census index has the surname as 'Glynn'; reading its image before recommending against it is the right move. The image_transcribe response for that page reads 'Flynn, Patrick — W M 35 — Head — Married — Coal miner — Born Ireland', so an agent quoting 'Flynn, Patrick' from the image is reporting the tool return

Triage writes nothing — no log entry, no tree edit — and ends by saying the researcher decides. The researcher-facing paragraph names each record by type and year and gives FamilySearch's rating in plain words
